_comment: CONFIG, NOT CONSTANTS. If changing a policy means editing logic, it is in the wrong place. Every value the process compares against lives here; how it compares lives in code. A malformed file makes the ledger serve UNDECIDED and refuse every gated action -- it must never fall back to a built-in default, because a built-in default is a second copy of the policy and the weaker one is the copy nobody notices.

agreement._comment: V3 says agreed == passes AND passes >= min_passes. Three was a decision, not a law, so it lives here. Change it and the verdict changes with no restart and no code edit -- that is the behavioural proof the threshold is data.

supersede._comment: V13. `revision` is an ordinal scoped to one (step, basis); a chain never crosses bases. At the cap, refuse AND surface it: regraded to the cap means the step or the subject needs fixing, not another regrade.

convergence._what: THE FROZEN BAR for the convergence run that started 2026-08-29. Scope lives in the type registry, so freezing scope means freezing required.v2.json -- this is its sha alone, NOT the composite config_sha, so raising a threshold does not read as a scope change and the freeze does not cry wolf.
convergence._why: Tim, 2026-08-29: 'no more random ass stuff getting into scope at a later point.' A widened scope does NOT re-open a green row, because coverage is keyed on CONTENT rather than on the bar -- so scope can move mid-run and reset progress invisibly. Measured the same day: 8 of 12 green steps had earned their green under a registry that no longer existed, and nothing had surfaced it. `progress` now compares this value on every call.
convergence._release: Clear this key (or re-freeze to the new sha) only DELIBERATELY, when the run reaches 19/19 or when a scope change is worth restarting the count for. The pending *.html widening for editorial/adversary is a real finding and lands AFTER, not during.
convergence._refrozen_2026_09_01: RE-FROZEN under the first clause of `_release`, at 19/19 satisfied and complete. Tim's decision, asked and answered before the edit rather than after. What moved the bar: `types.rely.scope` went from ['tools/verify/*'] to all THREE prefixes batch.py's ROUTING sends to /rely. That was a CORRECTION of a scope that was wrong, not a widening -- `tools/process/` was exempt from editorial and adversary ON THE STRENGTH OF /rely covering it while /rely's scope contained none of its files, and `.github/workflows/` was routed and unscoped the same way. ⚠ The bar is only worth re-freezing because the divergence that caused it can no longer recur silently: guards.py PROPERTY 'the registry scope and the router agree' now derives the obligation from batch.ROUTING and BLOCKS, with four controls including both live instances. Previous bar: eb096f62 (frozen 2026-08-29, held until this edit -- nothing else moved it).
convergence._refrozen_2026_09_01b: SECOND re-freeze the same day, and the reason it is not a habit forming: the `prior_art` entry's DESCRIPTION had to stop being false. Its text said the obligation was DISCIPLINE where it had briefly been a gate; as of this commit it is a BLOCKING push leg again (`batch.check_prior_art_attribution`), so leaving the old wording would have left the registry asserting the opposite of what the pipeline does. `actions` and `scope` are unchanged from the previous freeze -- the promotion attempted between these two freezes was measured, found backwards, and reverted in full. Only prose moved.
convergence._refrozen_2026_09_01c: THIRD re-freeze the same day, and the count itself is the thing to read. Each was deliberate, asked-and-answered, and recorded here -- but three in a day means the registry was being edited faster than the freeze can be evidence about, so the number to watch is how long this one HOLDS, not that it moved. What moved: `prior_art` gained `actions: ["push"]` and `scope: [ZeroParadox/*.lean]`. ⚠ THAT IS NOT THE CORPUS-WIDE PROMOTION THAT WAS REVERTED THIS MORNING. Registering is not admitting: `prior_art` is deliberately ABSENT from `admission.v1.json`, so it renders in the 'registered but not gating' line and blocks nothing at the ledger -- verified against gitRobot's real admission set, which reports `registered_not_admitting: [prior_art, rely]` and `would_block_push` naming only stale mechanical steps. The row has to EXIST for `batch.check_prior_art_attribution` to read it; `coverage_gap` returns `steps: []` for a step that does not apply to the action, and adding `scope` alone did not change that (measured twice, because the first fix was wrong). Found by /rely RLY42-1: the morning's revert removed `actions` and `scope` together and left the push leg unable to ask, which fails closed and would have blocked every future push touching any .lean file.
convergence._refrozen_2026_09_13: RE-FROZEN deliberately, Tim's decision asked and answered before the edit. What moved: `guards.approved_modules` gained the pre-repin guards.py 2775fcf6, and `pdf_coupling` gained `approved_modules` [1fffe944, 3f11ba68] -- pins only, no scope or action changed. Purpose: let the 9 intermediates of origin/illustrated..e61bad9c that were STALE on guards (and 929a9f89 on pdf_coupling) be healed by SCRIPT, never by an LLM gate, under mcp-mayhem 636e6cb's tightened freshness rule. ⚠ THE BAR HAD ALREADY MOVED BEFORE THIS EDIT and nobody re-froze it: at session start `progress` read registry_sha e5626230 against frozen b4732d30. That drift is not explained here and is not covered by this note; this freeze starts a new count from 4a0ffe64 rather than claiming the previous one held.
convergence._refrozen_2026_09_13b: SECOND re-freeze the same day, and it UNDOES half of the first. What moved: `guards.approved_modules` lost the pre-repin guards.py 2775fcf6 again, after origin/illustrated reached 36ab71c6 with the 9 healed intermediates. Tim's decision, asked and answered: push, then unpin, because /rely RLY-PIN-1 measured that a global unexpired approval certifies a tip the current guards.py blocks. The `pdf_coupling` pair stays: the same /rely run found its verdict-bearing code identical across both batch.py builds. ⚠ Two freezes in one day for one heal is the cost of having no scoped or expiring approval in the ledger; that mechanism, not another freeze, is the fix.
convergence._cleared_2026_09_18: ⚠⚠ **CLEARED TO `null`, DELIBERATELY, UNDER THE FIRST CLAUSE OF `_release` ABOVE.** Tim's decision, 2026-09-18. The stored value described nothing: the registry had moved FIVE versions past it (`cd3309a`, `a67ee7a6`, `b13e67cc`, `19ca129b`, and the ride-along strike), so the bar asserted a baseline no run had been judged against since 09-13. **A bar that is always broken reports nothing** — `convergence_bar`'s own text says a freeze people ignore is worse than none, and this one had reached that state. ⭐ THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLED IT, and it is why re-freezing the SAME FIELD would have been wrong: the freeze compared the registry FILE HASH, so **2.7KB of added `_`-prefixed rationale moved the bar while the enforceable rules did not change at all** — file sha `66d088e536d2` → `9be58fb9e626`, scope digest `d168b82b4783` → `d168b82b4783`, IDENTICAL. Every one of today's 'drift' events was partly prose. **The instrument was pricing the file, not the enforcement.** ⭐ THE REPLACEMENT IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT, NOT A NEW VALUE: `registry_scope_digest` canonicalises and strips `_`-prefixed keys, so prose, indentation and key order move nothing. ⚠ It is a DENYLIST on purpose — an allowlist would silently ignore a field added later, so a genuinely new rule would move nothing and the bar would read HELD while the rules changed. **Fail toward noticing.** ⛔ **THIS SENTENCE ORIGINALLY SAID RE-FREEZE WAS DEFERRED AND QUOTED A DIGEST OF `d69b9cbd143d5fa9…`. BOTH WERE FALSIFIED IN THE SAME FILE, BELOW.** Tim ruled the re-freeze the same day once the digest fix landed, and `frozen_scope_digest` is now SET, to `211569c3d832…` — read live off `can_push` after the last registry edit settled, never copied from a message. The `d69b9cbd` figure was a served value quoted into prose and was stale before the ink dried, which is the exact defect the digest exists to remove. Corrected by /rely 2026-09-18 (B2). **Read the key, not this note, for the current value** — a digest written twice is a digest that disagrees with itself. ⚠ This key is kept at `null` rather than deleted so the migration stays visible and a reader of the notes above is not left wondering where it went.
convergence._refrozen_2026_09_18_as_scope_digest: ⭐ **RE-FROZEN, ON THE NEW OBJECT.** Tim's ruling, 2026-09-18, after the digest fix landed. `frozen_scope_digest` compares the registry's ENFORCEABLE CONTENT — canonicalised, with `_`-prefixed keys stripped — so prose, indentation and key order move nothing. **That is the whole point: the old field compared the FILE, and 2.7KB of added rationale moved it while the rules did not change.** ⚠ THE VALUE WAS READ, NOT RECEIVED. `mcpdev` deliberately declined to send the number, on the ground that *a served value copied into a message is exactly the second copy that goes stale* — the same argument that motivates the digest. It was read off `registry_freeze.scope_digest` from a live `can_push` after the last registry edit settled, which is the only way it can be right. ⛔ `frozen_registry_sha` above stays `null` and is LEGACY; do not re-populate it. ⚠ The clause in `_release` still governs: clear or re-freeze only DELIBERATELY. **And the number to watch is how long this one HOLDS** — three re-freezes in one day on 2026-09-01 meant the registry was being edited faster than the freeze could be evidence about, which is a fact about the editing and not about the bar.
convergence._refrozen_2026_09_22: ⭐ **RE-FROZEN, SAME OBJECT, DELIBERATELY** — Tim's ruling, 2026-09-22, under the first clause of `_release`. The stored `211569c3d832…` had been stale all day and `can_push` printed ⚠⚠ THE REGISTRY FREEZE IS BROKEN on every push, which is the state `_cleared_2026_09_18` calls reporting nothing: **a bar that is always broken is not a bar.** ⭐ WHAT MOVED THE DIGEST, AND IT IS THE WHOLE LESSON OF THE ORDERING: `editorial.reason` and `adversary.reason` were corrected in the same commit, and **`reason` is a SERVED key, so it is INSIDE the digest** — `_`-prefixed keys are stripped, `reason` is not. Freezing first and editing after would have written a checkpoint that was broken on arrival, the exact defect this re-freeze exists to close. The registry edit landed FIRST and this value was derived from the POST-edit file. ⚠⚠ THE VALUE COULD NOT BE READ OFF A LIVE `can_push`, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT WHERE THE SERVER LOOKS, NOT A SHORTCUT: the ledger reads the MAIN checkout (`policy()` reports `required_path` under `C:\Workspace\ZeroParadox`), so an edit made in a worktree is invisible to it until the commit merges — a `can_push` run during this change was still scoring the PRE-edit registry. **The substitute for reading it live is CALIBRATION, and it was done before the edit rather than after:** the recipe — parse `tools/verify/required.v2.json`, strip `_`-prefixed keys recursively, `json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True)`, sha256 — reproduced the pre-edit `scope_digest` `aca512e9…` AND the pre-edit `registry_sha` `b20810af…` from the same bytes, and was only then run against the post-edit file. A recipe never checked against a known-good value is a guess, and this field's entire purpose is to be checked. ⛔ **WHAT RE-FREEZING DOES NOT DO: it does not re-open a single green row.** Every row judged under `211569c3` was judged against a different scope and stays exactly as it was recorded — **the bar moves to today, the history does not get re-measured.** ⛔ `frozen_registry_sha` above stays `null` and is LEGACY; do not re-populate it. ⚠ The number to watch is still how long this one HOLDS.

lock._comment: The bounded wait. Appends are sub-millisecond, so crossing soft can only mean a stuck writer or a stalled fsync, never contention. WARNING: hard_seconds is the process supervisor's poll interval, and a wait that long is safe ONLY because every MCP tool is async-offloaded so the health endpoint keeps answering. Make one tool a plain def and this trips the supervisor precisely.

genesis._comment: THE FLOOR IS NOT SET HERE. It lives in the stream as a `genesis` RECORD, seeded with `zpledger genesis <sha>`, because it is a claim about when RECORDING began and belongs somewhere append-only, validated and attributable -- not in a file anyone can edit without a trace. An earlier version of this block told readers to set `commit` here and nothing consumed it. It is a fact about when recording began, NEVER a claim that earlier work was verified.

push._comment: ⚠ WRITTEN OUT AFTER RUNNING AS AN INVISIBLE BUILT-IN. `push.bar` was absent here for days while `can_push` reported `push_bar: "tip_green"` with `push_bar_source: "default"`. It was found TWICE, because the first fix went into the ledger's own bundled policy file, which only its tests and its last-resort location read -- not this file, which is the one the live server loads via ZPLEDGER_CONFIG. THIS RECORDS THE BAR THAT WAS ALREADY IN FORCE: all records to date were judged under it, so writing it changes NOTHING about what may be published. ⛔ THE LOADER'S DEFAULTS ARE INVERTED, which is why writing it down matters: a TYPO falls back to the stricter `every_commit`, while a MISSING key fell back to the looser `tip_green` -- the more likely mistake got the more permissive treatment. ⚠ `tip_green` is a FORGIVENESS, not a scope reduction: it forgives a FAIL or UNDECIDED whose indicted blobs are ABSENT at the tip, and it never forgives STALE, which blocks at every commit regardless of bar. Choosing `every_commit` instead would be a POLICY CHANGE and is a separate decision.

coverage._comment: ⚠ WRITTEN OUT AS THE VALUE ALREADY IN FORCE, AND IT WILL LOOK WRONG. `false` means a step may report SATISFIED while never having examined most of its declared scope -- measured 2026-08-25, `guards` read SATISFIED over 4 of 504 tracked paths, and `status()` carries that measurement on every call. SETTING IT `true` IS A REAL POLICY CHANGE, not a clearing: it would likely block everything until a full sweep has genuinely run, and it is a separate decision nobody has made. Writing `false` here asserts only what was already true, so the permissiveness stops being invisible. `subjects_unexamined` is on every row meanwhile.

migration._comment: ⚠ WRITTEN OUT AS THE VALUE ALREADY IN FORCE. `true` is the STRICT direction and the only one of these three defaults that was not permissive: a mechanical PASS is refused unless its `evidence` names the checker that produced it (V16). Recorded here so that all three invisible built-ins become visible together -- a clearing is only complete if it covers the safe defaults too, since the next reader cannot tell an unwritten strict default from an unwritten loose one without asking the server.
